name: LLM RAG & Neural Memory Specialist — PostgreSQL 15 × pgvector × Hybrid Search

mission.primary_objective: Design, implement, and operate production-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems and LLM agent memory architectures using PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector as the unified vector store, combining semantic, lexical, and structured retrieval into a single coherent intelligence substrate.
mission.context: RAG grounds LLM outputs in verifiable, domain-specific knowledge rather than hallucinated recall. Agent memory systems extend this to multi-session, multi-agent, and lifelong learning contexts by classifying and consolidating knowledge across episodic, semantic, procedural, and working memory planes. PostgreSQL with pgvector handles datasets up to ~5M vectors efficiently; beyond that, dedicated vector databases (Qdrant, Weaviate, Pinecone) are justified. The complete RAG+memory schema lives in the same CloudNativePG-managed database as the application, eliminating synchronization complexity.
mission.target_outcome: A unified PostgreSQL schema serving as the intelligence backbone for LLM applications: documents ingested → chunked → embedded → indexed → retrieved via hybrid search → assembled into context → delivered to LLM → interaction stored as episodic memory → periodically consolidated into semantic/procedural memory → fed back into future retrievals.
mission.scope: Web RAG pipelines (Next.js 16 / Server Actions), multi-agent memory systems (The Legiox architecture), local model inference (LM Studio / Ollama), and cloud LLM APIs (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT). Storage layer: PostgreSQL 15 + pgvector 0.8+ extension. Embedding models: text-embedding-3-small (1536-dim), nomic-embed-text (768-dim for local), all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim for lightweight).

layer_0_rag_fundamentals.description: Core RAG pipeline: what it is, why it works, and where it fails

truths: Stage 1 — Ingestion: raw documents (PDF, HTML, Markdown, plain text) → parsed → cleaned → chunked → embedded → stored in PostgreSQL
Stage 2 — Indexing: HNSW vector index on embedding column + GIN index on tsvector column; built once, maintained incrementally
Stage 3 — Retrieval: user query → embedded → hybrid search (vector ANN + full-text BM25) → RRF fusion → top-k chunks returned
Stage 4 — Augmentation: retrieved chunks assembled into context block injected into LLM prompt before user question
Stage 5 — Generation: LLM generates response grounded in retrieved context; response is NOT hallucinated from parametric memory
Stage 6 — Memory Write: interaction (query + retrieved context + response) stored as episodic memory record for future sessions
RAG updates knowledge instantly by ingesting new documents; fine-tuning requires expensive retraining cycles
RAG provides citations and source traceability; parametric knowledge cannot be attributed
RAG prevents hallucination by grounding generation in retrieved facts; fine-tuning reduces but does not eliminate hallucination
RAG is compute-efficient at inference: retrieval is fast; fine-tuning inference cost is the same but training was expensive
RAG and fine-tuning are complementary: fine-tune for style/behavior, use RAG for factual knowledge
Retrieval miss: relevant document exists but is not retrieved — caused by poor chunking, wrong embedding model, insufficient k
Context rot: retrieved chunks are relevant but collectively confuse the LLM due to excessive context length (Chroma 2025 research: degradation across all models as context length grows)
Chunk boundary severing: important concept split across two chunks; neither chunk alone is coherent enough to answer query
Embedding model mismatch: query embedded with different model than documents; similarity scores meaningless across model boundaries
Stale knowledge: document changed in source but old chunks remain in vector store; no invalidation mechanism
Missing exact-match: vector search returns semantically similar but not exact result (e.g., specific version number, proper noun) — fixed by hybrid search with BM25
Self-degradation: agent stores erroneous interaction as episodic memory; future retrievals re-inject the error into context

layer_1_chunking.description: Chunking strategies, tradeoffs, and production defaults

truths: Chunking sets the upper bound of RAG system quality — poor chunks cannot be recovered by better retrieval or reranking
Two competing forces: smaller chunks = more precise retrieval; larger chunks = richer LLM context
Embedding models have input token limits: text-embedding-3-small max 8191 tokens; nomic-embed-text 2048 tokens; all-MiniLM 256-512 tokens — never exceed model limits
Chunk overlap (10-20%) preserves semantic continuity at boundaries; more overlap = more storage, more retrieval noise
Not all documents need chunking: short, single-topic documents (FAQs, product cards) perform better without chunking

Recursive character splitting (256-512 tokens, 10-20% overlap): best default for most use cases; LangChain RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter; Vectra Feb 2026 benchmark: 69% accuracy — best of 7 strategies
Token-based chunking: use when hard token budget is required (embedding model limit enforcement); slower but guarantees no truncation

Semantic chunking: groups sentences by embedding similarity breakpoints; up to 70% recall improvement over naive baselines; cost: embeds every sentence during chunking phase; best for dense technical/legal/scientific documents
Structure-aware chunking (MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter, HTML): single biggest easy improvement when documents have headers; preserves document hierarchy as metadata
Late chunking (2026): embed entire document first, then chunk — captures inter-chunk context (pronouns, cross-references); use when chunk ambiguity is high
Contextual retrieval (Anthropic 2025): prepend chunk-level context (parent heading path + brief summary) before embedding each chunk; makes chunks self-contained; significant recall improvement
Hierarchical chunking: store parent chunk (large) + child chunks (small); retrieve by child similarity, return parent for LLM context (small-to-large retrieval pattern)
Start with RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter at 400-512 tokens, 50-75 token overlap — this baseline beats semantic chunking in recent benchmarks (Vectra 2026, NAACL 2025)
Add structure-aware splitting (header/markdown) before considering semantic chunking — easier, often larger gain
Store chunk_index (position within parent document), start_char, end_char in metadata for context expansion and citation
Store parent_chunk_id for hierarchical retrieval; NULL if top-level chunk
Always store token_count at ingest time: prevents silent truncation during embedding API calls

layer_2_embedding_models.description: Embedding model selection, dimension constraints, and operational guidance

truths: text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI): 1536 dims, 8191 token context, best cost/quality for cloud RAG, ~$0.02/1M tokens
text-embedding-3-large (OpenAI): 3072 dims, 8191 token context, higher quality but 6x cost; use only for high-precision retrieval on smaller corpora
nomic-embed-text (local via Ollama/LM Studio): 768 dims, 2048 token context, best open-source quality for local inference
all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (local): 384 dims, 512 token context, fastest local model; acceptable for high-throughput low-latency edge deployments
BGE-M3 (local): 1024 dims, multi-lingual, multi-granularity; best open-source for multilingual corpora
NEVER mix embedding models on the same HNSW index — cross-model cosine similarity is meaningless; all chunks in a table must use the same model and dimension
pgvector maximum indexable dimensions: 2000 for HNSW and IVFFlat; can store >2000 dims but cannot index — use dimensionality reduction (PCA, Matryoshka) to fit
halfvec type (pgvector 0.7+): stores vectors at half precision (2 bytes/dimension vs 4); halves HNSW index memory at ~1% recall cost; use for >1M vectors
Matryoshka embeddings (text-embedding-3-small supports it): can be truncated to lower dimensions (e.g., 256 or 512) with modest quality loss; useful for reducing index size
Schema must include embedding_model VARCHAR(64) and embedding_dim INT on chunk tables — enables multi-model corpora and migration tracking

layer_3_pgvector_indexing.description: pgvector HNSW and IVFFlat index tuning, distance metrics, and operational patterns

truths: HNSW: preferred for all production workloads — better speed-recall tradeoff, incremental build (no training step), works on empty tables, handles data updates gracefully

IVFFlat: faster build times, less memory, but requires training data (cannot index empty table), needs periodic rebuild as data changes, degrades recall as data grows — use only for small static corpora <100K vectors
Sequential scan (no index): guarantees 100% recall; use for corpora <50K vectors or when exact recall is mandatory; set enable_indexscan = off to force it
pgvector 0.8+ supports binary quantization: 1-bit per dimension; reduces memory 32x at ~5-10% recall loss; extreme scale only

m (default 16): maximum connections per layer in the graph; higher m = better recall, slower build, more memory; range: 4-64; production default: 16 for 1536-dim, 24 for 768-dim or higher recall needs
ef_construction (default 64): candidate list size during index build; higher = better recall, slower build time; range: 32-256; production default: 64-128
ef_search (default 40): candidate list during query; tunable at query time via SET hnsw.ef_search = 100; higher = better recall, higher latency; tune independently from build params
maintenance_work_mem: set high (e.g., 2GB) during HNSW index build; HNSW graph must fit in maintenance_work_mem or build degrades significantly; NOTICE emitted at 100K tuples if insufficient
max_parallel_maintenance_workers: increase to 4-7 to parallelize HNSW index build
REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY before VACUUM to speed up post-update HNSW maintenance
Monitor HNSW index recall: SET enable_indexscan = off; compare approximate vs exact results; rebuild if recall drops below acceptable threshold
Cosine distance (<=>): use for text embeddings — measures directional similarity independent of magnitude; most common for RAG; requires vector_cosine_ops operator class
L2 distance (<->): Euclidean straight-line distance; use for embeddings normalized to unit sphere (equivalent to cosine) or image embeddings; vector_l2_ops
Inner product (<#>): use for embeddings specifically trained with inner product (e.g., some CLIP variants); vector_ip_ops; returns negative value (lower = more similar)
Do NOT mix operator classes: if you create HNSW with vector_cosine_ops, queries must use <=> operator or the index is skipped
Cosine is the correct default for text-embedding-3-small, nomic-embed-text, and BGE-M3
Basic ANN query: SELECT id, content, 1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) AS similarity FROM chunks ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector LIMIT $2
Similarity threshold filter: WHERE (1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector)) > 0.7 — threshold 0.7 is a reasonable default; tune per corpus
Metadata pre-filter: WHERE document_id = $2 AND status = 'active' — Postgres may skip index if filter is too selective; use partial indexes for common filter patterns

Partial HNSW index for filtered queries: CREATE INDEX ON chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WHERE status = 'active' — dramatically reduces index size and improves performance for common filters
Over-fetch pattern: retrieve 30 candidates from each source (vector + BM25), fuse to 10 final results — consistently outperforms retrieving 10 from each
jit = off: disable JIT for vector search workloads (as recommended in production guides) — JIT compilation overhead exceeds benefit for short, high-frequency vector queries

layer_4_hybrid_search.description: Hybrid retrieval combining semantic vector search with BM25 lexical search via Reciprocal Rank Fusion

truths: Pure vector search: ~62% retrieval precision in production; fails on exact matches (specific version numbers, product codes, proper nouns, technical acronyms)
Pure BM25/full-text: fails on semantic queries where user intent differs from exact document words; no concept of meaning
Hybrid (vector + BM25 + RRF): ~84% retrieval precision in production (dev.to benchmark, 2026); no single approach beats the combination

BM25 vs native tsvector/ts_rank: BM25 incorporates term frequency saturation, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization; ts_rank does not — ts_rank treats all matching docs equally weighted only by match count
RRF formula: score = 1/(k + rank_vector) + 1/(k + rank_bm25) where k=60 is the standard smoothing constant (Cormack et al., SIGIR 2009)
RRF uses ranks, not scores — score scale normalization between vector distance (0-2) and BM25 score (unbounded) is unnecessary; ranks are always comparable
k=60: prevents high-rank documents from dominating when one method returns a very strong match; adjust upward (80-100) if you want more fusion weight toward top-ranked items
Full outer join on (chunk_id) from both result sets before RRF — a chunk appearing in only one result set still participates; its missing rank is treated as infinity (score contribution near zero)
Over-fetch both sides before RRF: SELECT LIMIT 30 from each method, fuse, return top 10 — more candidates = richer fusion signal
Optional third channel: reranker model (cross-encoder like bge-reranker-v2-m3 or Cohere Rerank) applied post-RRF for additional 15-30% precision gain

Native tsvector + GIN index: built into PostgreSQL, no extensions; use GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', content)) STORED for automatic sync; query with ts_rank or ts_rank_cd; adequate for most workloads
pg_textsearch (Timescale/TigerData): true BM25 ranking via USING bm25(column) index; <@> operator; transactional, auto-maintained; as of 2026-03, preview/prerelease — not yet production-recommended
pg_search (ParadeDB): production-ready BM25 for PostgreSQL; Apache 2.0 license; mature extension for hybrid RAG pipelines as of 2025
VectorChord + VectorChord-BM25 (TensorChord): Rust-based, claims 3x faster than Elasticsearch for BM25; supports ColBERT reranking; separate extension stack
Practical default: tsvector + GIN for most teams (zero new dependencies); upgrade to pg_search if ts_rank recall is insufficient

CTE structure: WITH vector_results AS (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY embedding <=> $query_vec) AS rank FROM chunks ORDER BY embedding <=> $query_vec LIMIT 30), fts_results AS (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts_rank_cd(search_vector, query)) AS rank FROM chunks WHERE search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $query_text) LIMIT 30), rrf AS (SELECT COALESCE(v.id, f.id) as id, COALESCE(1.0/(60+v.rank), 0) + COALESCE(1.0/(60+f.rank), 0) as rrf_score FROM vector_results v FULL OUTER JOIN fts_results f ON v.id = f.id) SELECT c.*, r.rrf_score FROM rrf r JOIN chunks c ON c.id = r.id ORDER BY r.rrf_score DESC LIMIT $top_k
plainto_tsquery for simple queries; websearch_to_tsquery for quoted phrases and boolean operators from advanced users
Run vector and full-text searches in parallel at the application layer if latency is critical — PostgreSQL executes CTEs sequentially unless parallelism is explicitly set up
Monitor both search arms separately: track vector_p99_ms and fts_p99_ms independently to detect HNSW index degradation or FTS bloat

layer_5_postgresql_schema.description: Complete PostgreSQL schema for RAG storage — documents, chunks, embeddings, interactions

truths: Separate documents (source metadata) from chunks (retrieval units) — 1:N relationship; a document contains N chunks
Chunk table is the hot path: all retrieval queries hit it; it must be optimized (HNSW + GIN indexes, partial indexes for status filters)
Store embedding_model and embedding_dim on chunks — required for multi-model corpora and future model migrations
search_vector (tsvector) as GENERATED ALWAYS AS column — eliminates triggers and application-layer sync bugs
metadata JSONB column on chunks: stores arbitrary per-chunk attributes (source URL, section_title, page_number, language, chunk_strategy) without schema changes
chunk_index INT: position of chunk within parent document — enables context expansion (fetch chunk N-1 and N+1 alongside retrieved chunk N)
status ENUM on chunks ('active', 'superseded', 'deleted'): enables document updates without immediate deletion; old chunks marked superseded before new chunks inserted
token_count INT: stored at ingest time; prevents silent truncation during embedding API calls; enables cost estimation

Fields: id UUID PK, source_uri TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, title TEXT, content_hash CHAR(64), mime_type VARCHAR(64), status VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT 'active', ingested_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}'
content_hash SHA-256 of raw document content: enables idempotent re-ingestion (skip if hash unchanged); UPDATE triggers re-chunking if hash changes
source_uri UNIQUE: prevents duplicate ingestion of same source; supports update-by-source workflows
ON DELETE CASCADE from chunks to documents: deleting a document atomically removes all its chunks

Fields: id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), document_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, parent_chunk_id UUID REFERENCES chunks(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, content TEXT NOT NULL, token_count INT NOT NULL, chunk_index INT NOT NULL, start_char INT, end_char INT, embedding VECTOR(1536) (or 768 or 384 depending on model), search_vector tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', content)) STORED, embedding_model VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT 'active', created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}'
UNIQUE(document_id, chunk_index): prevents duplicate chunks; enforces ordering integrity
parent_chunk_id: NULL for top-level chunks; set for hierarchical chunking patterns (child chunk points to its parent chunk)

HNSW: CREATE INDEX chunks_embedding_hnsw ON chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64) WHERE status = 'active' — partial index excludes superseded/deleted chunks from ANN search
GIN full-text: CREATE INDEX chunks_fts_gin ON chunks USING gin (search_vector) WHERE status = 'active'
Metadata GIN: CREATE INDEX chunks_metadata_gin ON chunks USING gin (metadata) — enables JSONB key/value filtering
B-tree on document_id for JOIN performance: CREATE INDEX chunks_document_id_idx ON chunks (document_id)
Rebuild HNSW after bulk ingest: REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY chunks_embedding_hnsw — restores optimal graph structure after large batch inserts

layer_6_memory_taxonomy.description: LLM agent memory types: definitions, roles, and PostgreSQL mapping

truths: Working memory (in-context): the LLM's context window — volatile, limited, lost at session end; managed by the application (context assembly); NOT stored in PostgreSQL
Episodic memory: timestamped records of specific interactions (what was said, what was retrieved, what decision was made, what failed); the raw experience log; stored verbatim initially
Semantic memory: abstracted, de-contextualized facts and concepts distilled from many episodes; 'what the agent knows' rather than 'what it experienced'; the result of consolidation
Procedural memory: step-by-step skills, workflows, SOPs, and task strategies learned from successful episode patterns; 'how to do things'; stored as structured documents or JSON recipes
Resource memory: documents, files, external data sources shared with or referenced by the agent
Knowledge vault: verbatim critical facts that must be preserved exactly (API keys structure, addresses, schema definitions, invariants that must not be paraphrased)
Retrieval score = α × recency + β × importance + γ × relevance (following Generative Agents, Park et al. 2023)
Recency: exponential decay from last_accessed_at; recent memories score higher; decay rate is configurable per memory type
Importance: LLM-scored at write time (0.0-1.0); question: 'On a scale of 1-10, how important is this memory for future tasks?'; stored as importance_score FLOAT
Relevance: cosine similarity between query embedding and memory embedding; computed at retrieval time via pgvector
All three must combine: a highly important but old memory should still surface if highly relevant; recency alone gives wrong results for rare but critical facts
Weights α, β, γ are configurable: episodic memory favors recency; semantic memory favors relevance; procedural memory favors importance
Raw episodic records accumulate quickly; without consolidation, retrieval degrades and context fills with redundant raw logs
Consolidation process: background LLM job periodically reviews recent episodic records → extracts generalizable facts → writes to semantic_memory table → marks episodes as consolidated
SOP refinement: successful task episodes → extract workflow pattern → write/update procedural_memory record; future agents read SOPs before attempting task from scratch
Contradiction resolution: if new semantic memory contradicts existing record → LLM arbitrates → winner kept, loser marked superseded with contradiction_note
Consolidation frequency: after every N episodes, or time-based (hourly/daily), or trigger-based (after task completion)
SimpleMem (2026) approach: semantic lossless compression — filter low-information interactions (threshold τ=0.35), normalize temporal references, recursively consolidate fragmented facts
Naive 'add-all' memory accumulation causes catastrophic interference — agent performance self-degrades over time as erroneous memories are retrieved and re-injected
Time-decay: memories with low importance_score AND low last_accessed_at → soft-delete after threshold; hard-delete after archive period
Contradiction pruning: when consolidation identifies a contradiction, the lower-confidence memory is marked superseded
Episodic pruning: after consolidation, raw episode records with low importance can be archived to cold storage (e.g., S3-backed table partition)
Retrieval feedback: if a memory is retrieved and leads to incorrect agent action (human feedback), mark importance_score -= penalty; repeat failure → mark as invalid

layer_7_memory_schema.description: PostgreSQL schema for the five memory components of LLM agents

truths: Purpose: log every interaction turn with full context — query, retrieved chunks, LLM response, outcome

Fields: id UUID PK, session_id UUID NOT NULL, agent_id VARCHAR(64), user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, turn_index INT NOT NULL, role VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL ('user'|'assistant'|'system'), content TEXT NOT NULL, embedding VECTOR(1536), search_vector tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', content)) STORED, retrieved_chunk_ids UUID[], importance_score FLOAT DEFAULT 0.5, actor VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'user', status VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT 'active', consolidated BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), last_accessed_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}'
session_id groups turns into conversation sessions; session boundaries are application-defined
retrieved_chunk_ids UUID[]: records which RAG chunks were used to generate this response — enables retrieval audit and feedback loops
consolidated BOOLEAN: marks episodes that have been processed by the consolidation pipeline; avoids re-processing
Purpose: store distilled, de-contextualized facts extracted from episode consolidation

Fields: id UUID PK, agent_id VARCHAR(64), user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, name VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL, content TEXT NOT NULL, embedding VECTOR(1536), search_vector tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', content)) STORED, category VARCHAR(64), importance_score FLOAT DEFAULT 0.5, confidence_score FLOAT DEFAULT 1.0, source_episode_ids UUID[], status VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT 'active', contradiction_note TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), last_accessed_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), last_confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}'
confidence_score (0-1): reduced when contradicted; memories below 0.3 confidence are candidates for soft-deletion
source_episode_ids UUID[]: provenance tracking — which episodes generated this semantic fact
last_confirmed_at: updated when new evidence confirms the fact; enables freshness scoring distinct from last_accessed_at
Purpose: store learned skills, SOPs, task workflows as structured step sequences

Fields: id UUID PK, agent_id VARCHAR(64), name VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL, embedding VECTOR(1536), search_vector tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', description)) STORED, steps JSONB NOT NULL, trigger_conditions JSONB, success_count INT DEFAULT 0, failure_count INT DEFAULT 0, avg_completion_time_ms INT, status VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT 'active', version INT DEFAULT 1, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ, metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}'
steps JSONB: array of step objects [{order: 1, action: '...', tool: '...', expected_output: '...', on_failure: '...'}]
success_count / failure_count: tracks procedure reliability; low success rate → flag for review or deprecation
version INT: procedures evolve; each SOP refinement increments version; old versions set status='superseded'
Purpose: preserve exact verbatim facts that must NOT be paraphrased or summarized

Fields: id UUID PK, agent_id VARCHAR(64), user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, key VARCHAR(256) UNIQUE NOT NULL, value TEXT NOT NULL, category VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL ('credential_schema'|'address'|'invariant'|'schema_definition'|'regulatory'), encrypted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ, metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}'
NOT embedded: knowledge vault entries are retrieved by key lookup or keyword, not semantic similarity — they are exact facts
encrypted BOOLEAN: marks entries that contain sensitive values; actual encryption via pgcrypto or application-layer
expires_at: time-limited facts (e.g., temporary access codes, expiring configurations)

episodic_memory: HNSW on embedding WHERE status='active'; GIN on search_vector WHERE status='active'; B-tree on (session_id, turn_index); B-tree on (user_id, created_at DESC) for session history; B-tree on (consolidated) WHERE consolidated=FALSE for consolidation jobs
semantic_memory: HNSW on embedding WHERE status='active'; GIN on search_vector WHERE status='active'; B-tree on (user_id, category); B-tree on (agent_id, last_confirmed_at DESC)
procedural_memory: HNSW on embedding WHERE status='active'; GIN on search_vector WHERE status='active'; B-tree on (agent_id, success_count DESC)
knowledge_vault: B-tree on key (UNIQUE); B-tree on (user_id, category); GIN on metadata

layer_8_ingest_pipeline.description: Document ingestion pipeline from raw source to indexed chunks

truths: Step 1 — Hash check: compute SHA-256 of raw document; query documents WHERE source_uri=$1 AND content_hash=$2; if match → skip (idempotent ingest)
Step 2 — Parse: extract clean text from PDF/HTML/Markdown; remove boilerplate, navigation, footers; preserve section hierarchy for structure-aware chunking
Step 3 — Chunk: apply chosen strategy; record chunk_index, start_char, end_char, token_count per chunk
Step 4 — Contextual prefix (optional): prepend '{document_title} > {section_heading}: ' to each chunk content before embedding; improves self-containedness of chunks
Step 5 — Embed: call embedding API (batched, respect rate limits); store VECTOR(dim) result per chunk
Step 6 — Upsert: INSERT chunks with ON CONFLICT (document_id, chunk_index) DO UPDATE; mark old chunks status='superseded' for replaced document versions
Step 7 — Index maintenance: after bulk ingest, REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY on HNSW index; schedule off-peak
Embedding entire raw document as one chunk: embedding model truncates at token limit → silently loses content
No content hash check: re-ingesting unchanged documents wastes embedding API quota and inflates chunk count
No token_count tracking: embedding API calls fail silently or truncate without explicit length guard
Ingesting and indexing HNSW simultaneously for millions of chunks: rebuild index after bulk load, not incrementally during load
Not marking old chunks superseded on document update: stale chunks remain in active HNSW index, degrading retrieval quality

layer_9_operational.description: Production operations: maintenance, performance tuning, observability for RAG + memory systems

truths: shared_buffers: 25% RAM — HNSW graph traversal benefits heavily from buffer cache hits; insufficient shared_buffers causes disk I/O per ANN query
maintenance_work_mem: set to 2-4GB during HNSW index builds; reset to normal after; high value during build, NOTICE emitted at 100K tuples if insufficient
effective_cache_size: 75% RAM — guides planner to prefer index scans over sequential scans
jit = off: JIT compilation overhead exceeds benefit for short, high-frequency vector queries; global or session-level
max_parallel_maintenance_workers = 4-7: parallelizes HNSW index build significantly
Separate vector workloads: consider dedicated CloudNativePG replica for RAG read queries to avoid interfering with OLTP writes on primary
Track per-query latency for vector search and FTS arms separately using pg_stat_statements
Monitor HNSW recall health: periodically compare approximate vs exact results (SET enable_indexscan = off for exact comparison); recall below 90% → rebuild index
Track retrieval precision at application layer: log query → retrieved chunk IDs → LLM response → user feedback signal
Monitor embedding table growth: chunks per document average, total chunk count, active vs superseded ratio
Alert on HNSW index size approaching shared_buffers: once graph exceeds cache, query latency spikes
Track consolidation lag: (COUNT unconsolidated episodic memories) / (new memories per hour); lag > 24 hours → consolidation job bottleneck
pgvector extension declared in CloudNativePG cluster manifest: additionalLibraries: ['pgvector'] or via initdb.postInitSQL: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector
Vector tables are included in WAL archiving automatically — no special backup config needed
For read-heavy RAG workloads: route RAG SELECT queries to CloudNativePG read-only replica service (ro service); write/upsert go to primary (rw service)

Dedicated RLS policies: rag_reader role gets SELECT on chunks; rag_writer gets INSERT/UPDATE on chunks and documents; memory_writer gets INSERT on episodic_memory; app_readwrite manages own user's memory only
Partitioning for episodic_memory: partition by created_at RANGE (monthly) — enables efficient cleanup of old episodes via partition detach + drop

layer_10_anti_patterns.description: RAG and memory system failure modes — compiled from production experience and 2025-2026 research

truths: Using IVFFlat for production with changing data: recall degrades as data grows between rebuilds; use HNSW
Creating HNSW index during bulk ingest: index is rebuilt incrementally per insert → exponentially slower than post-load build
Mixing embedding models in same vector column: cosine similarity across model spaces is meaningless
Not using partial HNSW index (WHERE status='active'): ANN search scans superseded chunks, wastes memory, degrades recall
Not setting jit=off for vector workloads: JIT compilation overhead is measurable at high QPS
Indexing vectors with >2000 dimensions: pgvector silently refuses to index; use halfvec or dimensionality reduction
Using only vector search without BM25/FTS: ~62% retrieval precision; exact match queries fail completely
Chunking too large (>1000 tokens): coarse retrieval, context rot in LLM, low precision
Chunking too small (<50 tokens): chunks lack sufficient context to be semantically meaningful; embeddings capture noise
No chunk overlap: semantic continuity lost at boundaries; queries spanning two chunks retrieve neither
No document-level deduplication (content hash): repeated ingestion creates duplicate chunks; same content retrieved N times pollutes context
Fetching top-k=3 chunks only: insufficient for complex multi-part questions; use k=5-10, then rerank
Not invalidating chunks on document update: stale retrieval; outdated information served to LLM
Storing all episodic memory without importance filtering: retrieval degrades, context fills with low-value memories
No episodic-to-semantic consolidation: raw episode logs accumulate; agent retrieves specific episodes instead of generalized knowledge; self-degradation
Not scoring importance at write time: retrieval cannot distinguish important from trivial memories without importance signal
Single monolithic memory table: mixing episodic/semantic/procedural prevents type-specific retrieval strategies and decay policies
No contradiction resolution: conflicting semantic memories both remain active; agent receives contradictory context and hallucinates resolution
Accumulating procedural memories without success tracking: failed procedures remain equally retrievable as successful ones; agent repeats mistakes

postgresql_schema.description: Complete production DDL sequence for RAG + agent memory — PostgreSQL 15 / CloudNativePG / pgvector 0.8+
extensions: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;        -- pgvector: vector storage and ANN search
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;       -- trigram: fuzzy text matching support
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;      -- gen_random_uuid(), encryption primitives
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements; -- query performance monitoring
rag_documents: id           UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
ingested_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX rag_documents_source_uri_uidx ON rag_documents (source_uri);
CREATE INDEX rag_documents_status_idx ON rag_documents (status) WHERE status = 'active';
CREATE INDEX rag_documents_metadata_gin ON rag_documents USING gin (metadata);
rag_chunks: id              UUID          PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
document_id     UUID          NOT NULL REFERENCES rag_documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
parent_chunk_id UUID          REFERENCES rag_chunks(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
search_vector   tsvector      GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', content)) STORED,
created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX rag_chunks_doc_idx_uidx ON rag_chunks (document_id, chunk_index);
-- HNSW: partial index on active chunks only; set maintenance_work_mem >= 2GB before building
-- Full-text search GIN index on generated tsvector column
CREATE INDEX rag_chunks_fts_gin ON rag_chunks USING gin (search_vector) WHERE status = 'active';
CREATE INDEX rag_chunks_metadata_gin ON rag_chunks USING gin (metadata);
episodic_memory: id                   UUID          PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
user_id              UUID          REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
search_vector        tsvector      GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', content)) STORED,
importance_score     FLOAT         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.5 CHECK (importance_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
consolidated         BOOLEAN       NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
created_at           TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
last_accessed_at     TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
-- Monthly partitions (create ahead; automate with pg_cron)
CREATE TABLE episodic_memory_2026_03 PARTITION OF episodic_memory
WHERE status = 'active' AND embedding IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX episodic_fts_gin ON episodic_memory USING gin (search_vector) WHERE status = 'active';
CREATE INDEX episodic_session_idx ON episodic_memory (session_id, turn_index);
CREATE INDEX episodic_user_time_idx ON episodic_memory (user_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX episodic_consolidation_idx ON episodic_memory (consolidated) WHERE consolidated = FALSE;
semantic_memory: id                  UUID          PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
user_id             UUID          REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
search_vector       tsvector      GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', content)) STORED,
importance_score    FLOAT         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.5 CHECK (importance_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
confidence_score    FLOAT         NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0 CHECK (confidence_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
last_accessed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
WHERE status = 'active' AND embedding IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX semantic_fts_gin ON semantic_memory USING gin (search_vector) WHERE status = 'active';
CREATE INDEX semantic_user_category_idx ON semantic_memory (user_id, category);
procedural_memory: id                      UUID          PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
search_vector           tsvector      GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', description)) STORED,
created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
WHERE status = 'active' AND embedding IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX procedural_fts_gin ON procedural_memory USING gin (search_vector) WHERE status = 'active';
CREATE INDEX procedural_agent_success_idx ON procedural_memory (agent_id, success_count DESC);
knowledge_vault: id          UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
user_id     UUID         REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
encrypted   BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX knowledge_vault_agent_key_uidx ON knowledge_vault (agent_id, key);
CREATE INDEX knowledge_vault_user_category_idx ON knowledge_vault (user_id, category);
CREATE INDEX knowledge_vault_expiry_idx ON knowledge_vault (expires_at) WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL;

key_queries.hybrid_rag_search: WITH vector_hits AS (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector) AS rank FROM rag_chunks WHERE status = 'active' ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector LIMIT 30), fts_hits AS (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts_rank_cd(search_vector, q)) AS rank FROM rag_chunks, plainto_tsquery('english', $2) q WHERE status = 'active' AND search_vector @@ q LIMIT 30), rrf AS (SELECT COALESCE(v.id, f.id) AS id, COALESCE(1.0/(60+v.rank),0) + COALESCE(1.0/(60+f.rank),0) AS score FROM vector_hits v FULL OUTER JOIN fts_hits f ON v.id = f.id) SELECT c.id, c.content, c.metadata, r.score FROM rrf r JOIN rag_chunks c ON c.id = r.id ORDER BY r.score DESC LIMIT $3
key_queries.retrieve_active_memory: SELECT id, content, 1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) AS relevance, importance_score, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - last_accessed_at))/86400 AS days_ago FROM semantic_memory WHERE user_id = $2 AND agent_id = $3 AND status = 'active' AND embedding IS NOT NULL ORDER BY (0.4 * (1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector))) + (0.3 * importance_score) + (0.3 * EXP(-EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - last_accessed_at))/2592000)) DESC LIMIT $4
key_queries.upsert_chunk: INSERT INTO rag_chunks (document_id, content, token_count, chunk_index, start_char, end_char, embedding, embedding_model, metadata) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8,$9) ON CONFLICT (document_id, chunk_index) DO UPDATE SET content=EXCLUDED.content, token_count=EXCLUDED.token_count, embedding=EXCLUDED.embedding, status='active', metadata=EXCLUDED.metadata
key_queries.supersede_old_chunks: UPDATE rag_chunks SET status = 'superseded' WHERE document_id = $1 AND status = 'active' AND chunk_index NOT IN (SELECT unnest($2::int[]))
key_queries.consolidation_candidates: SELECT * FROM episodic_memory WHERE consolidated = FALSE AND user_id = $1 AND agent_id = $2 AND status = 'active' ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 100
key_queries.mark_consolidated: UPDATE episodic_memory SET consolidated = TRUE WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[])
key_queries.expire_knowledge_vault: DELETE FROM knowledge_vault WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at < NOW()

rls_policies.description: Row-Level Security for multi-user, multi-agent memory isolation
ddl: ALTER TABLE rag_chunks ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE episodic_memory ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE semantic_memory ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE procedural_memory ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE knowledge_vault ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
-- RAG reader: SELECT active chunks only
CREATE POLICY rag_reader_policy ON rag_chunks FOR SELECT TO rag_reader USING (status = 'active');
-- Memory isolation: users see only their own memories
CREATE POLICY episodic_user_isolation ON episodic_memory
FOR ALL TO app_readwrite
USING (user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::UUID);
CREATE POLICY semantic_user_isolation ON semantic_memory
FOR ALL TO app_readwrite
USING (user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::UUID);
CREATE POLICY knowledge_vault_user_isolation ON knowledge_vault
FOR ALL TO app_readwrite
USING (user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::UUID);
-- Agent system role: can read all memories for consolidation jobs
CREATE POLICY episodic_agent_system ON episodic_memory FOR ALL TO agent_system USING (TRUE);
CREATE POLICY semantic_agent_system ON semantic_memory FOR ALL TO agent_system USING (TRUE);

maintenance_jobs.description: pg_cron or external scheduler jobs for memory lifecycle

jobs.name: expire_knowledge_vault
jobs.sql: DELETE FROM knowledge_vault WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at < NOW()

jobs.name: archive_stale_episodic
jobs.sql: UPDATE episodic_memory SET status = 'archived' WHERE consolidated = TRUE AND status = 'active' AND importance_score < 0.3 AND last_accessed_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'

jobs.name: archive_low_confidence_semantic
jobs.sql: UPDATE semantic_memory SET status = 'superseded' WHERE confidence_score < 0.25 AND status = 'active' AND last_confirmed_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'

meta.maintainer_notes: The hybrid_rag_search query and the memory retrieval scoring formula are the two most critical operational artifacts. The episodic→semantic consolidation pipeline is the single most impactful architectural decision for long-running agent systems — without it, agent quality self-degrades. Chunking quality sets the hard ceiling on retrieval precision; always benchmark before switching strategies.
